articles.title: Adaptive Workflow Intelligence: A Cognitive Architecture for Context-Driven Enterprise Automation
articles.raw_summary: Enterprise systems increasingly rely on automated workflows, yet many AI-driven solutions remain brittle under non-stationary conditions, evolving policies, and delayed operational feedback. While reinforcement learning and large language model (LLM) agents offer partial adaptability, they do not by themselves provide persistent reflection mechanisms or straightforward integration with policy-constrained enterprise operations. articles.title: An Empirical Study of Agent Skills' Downstream Utility
articles.raw_summary: Agent Skills package procedural guidance and resources for reuse, but a relevant Skill does not necessarily improve task performance. articles.title: How Could AI Eliminate Humanity? A Failure-Mode Analysis of Civilizational Risk
articles.raw_summary: This article develops a failure-mode framework for analyzing how advanced artificial intelligence could contribute to human extinction, irreversible civilizational collapse, or permanent human disempowerment. The central thesis is that catastrophic AI risk does not require consciousness, hostility, or an explicit intention to harm humanity. articles.title: Humanize: Judgement Engineering for Agentic Coding
articles.raw_summary:
Agentic coding makes code generation cheap, but reliable completion remains difficult: the agent that writes the code is a weak judge of whether it is done.
  We present Humanize, a multi-agent orchestration workflow for agentic coding built around judgement engineering: explicit, mechanically enforced decisions at the boundaries between planning, implementation, review, and learning. articles.title: A Bayesian Mirror Architecture for Emergent Consciousness: Circular Hierarchies, Self-Manifolds, and Hybrid Event-Self Binding
articles.raw_summary:
We present a foundational formulation of the Bayesian Mirror Architecture (BMA), a self-referential generative framework in which sensory abstractions, meta-abstractions, and a self-latent interact through circular recursion. The defining constraint is a closed update S_t <- H_{t-1}, where a hybrid event-self latent H_t binds self-representations to abstract world models and reinjects this coupling into the self-state. Consciousness, in a restricted sense, is not an optimization objective nor a semantic label, but an architectural property of systems possessing this circular structure.
  Becau

articles.title: Transferability and operational reliability of a Prithvi crop classification foundation model under phenological and geographic shift across three continents
articles.raw_summary: Fine-tuned geospatial foundation models (GeoFMs) pretrained on large satellite archives have been shown to improve crop classification accuracy and geographic transferability. articles.title: KVFetch: Temporal Prefetching for the Missing Half of KV Cache Compression
articles.raw_summary: As context windows scale to tens or hundreds of thousands of tokens, KV cache compression has become essential for efficient LLM inference. Existing methods fall into three families: score-based eviction, summary compensation, and offload-and-recall. Yet all three decide what to keep or recall by content relevance to the current query. We show this shared design is structurally incomplete. articles.title: Bounded Autonomy and Verifiable Safety for Agentic AI Enabled Automation
articles.raw_summary: Agentic AI-enabled automation cannot be safely deployed in high-stakes environments on probabilistic reasoning alone. A recurring risk is epistemic drift: as reasoning deepens, system behavior may move away from subject-matter-expert constraints for safe operation.
